text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Greek Foreign Minister Thedoros Pangalos will visit Belgrade on Wednesday.
- Talks on economic succession of the former Yugoslavia started in international High Representative Carl Bildt's office in Brussels grouping delegations of all former Yugoslav states.
- Yugoslav political and economic delegation, headed by Deputy Prime Minister Jovan Zebic, is visiting Argentina and Brazil.
- Serbian exports will reach $2 billion by the end of the year, says Serbian minister coordinator Dragan Tomic.

- Foreign debts of all banks and firms as of August 20 stood at $6.6 billion, of which the National Bank holds 3.46 billion. Foreign claims stood at $1.98 billion, according to the National Bank of Yugoslavia.
- The daily Politika is the most widely read paper in Yugoslavia according to a poll conducted by public opinion firm Mark-plan.
- Direct bus line between Belgrade and Sarajevo started running Monday. First bus from Belgrade welcomed in Sarajevo with applause.
- Bosnian Serb National Assembly will hold a constituent session on Saturday, October 19.
- The EU has authorised export of livestock and meat from Yugoslavia from November 2, says Yugoslav agriculture minister Tihomir Vrebalov.

- The Pancevo oil refinery daily refines between seven and a half and nine thousand tonnes of oil, expects to maintain good supply of the market especially in diesel oil which is necessary for autumn agricultural works.

- Yugoslav insurance firms will pay the first part of their debt to the international car insurer's office by the end of the month. They agreed to repay the debt in four installments over a two-year period.
- Yugoslav airlines JAT introducing winter flight schedule from October 27 to March 29. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 43 05
